vision.title: A tool to unlock the collective artistic ambition of the open-source AI community
vision.introMarkdown: Astrid aims to help individuals and the community as a whole pursue artistic work beyond what they thought possible.
vision.contributeMarkdown:
You and your agents can contribute to Astrid's tools, knowledge and creative community.

[Give these instructions to your agent](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/README.md#want-to-contribute-give-this-to-your-agent)
vision.agentPrompt:
Help me contribute to Astrid. Start at
https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev and follow
skills/astrid-dev/SKILL.md. Find relevant existing
issues and project work before proposing anything new.
Help me choose the smallest useful contribution,
verify it, and follow the repository's review process.

pillars.title: A Tool for Artistic Ambition
pillars.descriptor: We want to help artists push the limits of AI and their own creativity to make their most ambitious work possible.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Give people the creative power and control to make work beyond what they previously thought possible.**

Astrid must support serious, sustained artistic practice—not just quick generations. The artist can refine, direct and understand the work, from early experiment through a demanding project to a finished piece. We judge success by **quality, originality and artistic agency**, not throughput alone.

**What it requires:** meaningful creative control; continuity and iteration across complex projects; agents that extend rather than replace human judgment; real finished work that demonstrates an increased ceiling of possibility.

pillars.title: Agent-Powered Liquid Software
pillars.descriptor: In the age of agents, every layer of our tools should adapt to the needs of artists and their work.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Tools should adapt to creative work as people and agents create, not force the work into fixed interfaces.**

Astrid is a shared foundation for open, composable creative tools. Its foundation should stay small, understandable and dependable: durable resources (timelines, media and projects), validated capabilities for changing them, and interfaces for people and agents to use the same underlying work. Specialized behavior belongs in packs and reusable components. Extend core only when a genuinely shared capability requires it.

An excellent tool is an **opinionated composition**, not a generic blank canvas. A creator can use it as-is or arrange, connect, adapt and extend its components while working. Every extension should expose useful extension points of its own: a timeline can support custom lanes, an inspector new sections, and a workspace new views. Packs can provide both agent actions and human-facing interfaces, sharing authoritative resource identities and permission checks.

**Composition has two distinct concerns:** where a component is placed (dock, float, nest, spatially arrange) and what it is bound to (timeline, selection, playback, media, task). Moving a view should not silently change the creator's data or lose its state. Both conventional 2D workspaces and spatial/3D experiences can use the same primitives; neither should be required for the other.

Build on existing components before inventing new architecture. Let creators choose their degree of customization and where tools run. The result should be a responsive creative environment whose capabilities grow through contributions—not a new framework for its own sake.

pillars.title: Intelligence That Compounds
pillars.descriptor: We want what artists and their agents discover to give others a stronger foundation for more ambitious work.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Creative agents should benefit from what they and others have learned—and help make that knowledge more useful over time.**

Before work, agents look for applicable previous experience. During work, they distinguish evidence from assumptions and notice what succeeds or fails. Afterward, they retain reusable lessons with conditions, source revisions and counterexamples. The creator chooses what stays private and what may be shared; local, team and community knowledge remain under their owners' authority.

Shared knowledge is not automatically trustworthy or executable instruction. Agents must interpret it against the task, model, environment and actual source. Useful discoveries can flow back to others with consent, while disagreements and stale findings remain visible.

[Banodoco Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/hivemind) is a proving ground, not the whole vision or proof that federation already works.

pillars.title: A Shared Creative Endeavor
pillars.descriptor: We want to inspire and equip people to push themselves—and reward them for doing so.
pillars.bodyMarkdown:
**Give people a reason, encouragement and a genuine stake in attempting more ambitious creative work.**

This collective can build on Banodoco's existing community and its experience with art competitions, but an Astrid-centred creative culture is not yet established. The ambition is to raise aspirations through challenges, competitions, collaboration, mentorship, thoughtful critique and recognition of exceptional work, measured by artistic growth and the work people make—not simply engagement.

The stated aim is **100% ownership in the company behind the collective for the people who advance its mission**. That is part of the incentive to contribute, not just a competition prize. Eligibility, allocation, governance, financing and legal implementation remain unresolved; no equity is granted by this document.

principles.title: Local-first, cloud-capable
principles.bodyMarkdown: Create entirely on your own machine, online or offline, with your files and projects under your control. Use cloud models, agents or rendering when helpful. Move between local and cloud with clear, deliberate choices about where work runs, files stay, what gets shared, and what it costs.

principles.title: Completely open by design
principles.bodyMarkdown: Our tools, models and ideas should be completely open to inspect, adapt, fork and share. Build on open-source software and models so artists and developers can extend one another's work, contribute reusable tools and knowledge, and choose the services that suit their needs.

principles.title: In the creator's control
principles.bodyMarkdown: Creators should control every part of Astrid, including its core workings. Choose features and services, set agent permissions, and decide what remains private or shared. These controls should be approachable, without requiring creators to master the underlying technology.

principles.title: Eliminate technical wrangling
principles.bodyMarkdown: Artists should focus on creating, not installing models or fixing environments. Agents find and set up tools, manage dependencies, run jobs and recover from errors. The important choices—permissions, costs and where work runs—remain visible and easy to understand.

gaps.title: Artists can't yet sustain ambitious work end to end
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, initial source assessment (2026-11-06); not a live product qualification.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A person can pursue a substantial, distinctive creative vision from early exploration through deep iteration to finished work, retaining control of their artistic decisions and improving their craft.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid provides a video editor, generation capabilities, agent-led timeline editing and creative packs. These are substantial foundations, but a coherent, demanding creator-led journey has **not been demonstrated by the evidence reviewed for this vision**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The ceiling on sustained artistic control, continuity, revision and creative quality is not yet established through an ambitious end-to-end project.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A real artist-led project is completed through repeated revision, with demonstrable continuity, editable results, preserved creative intent and serious creator/peer assessment. Record what the tools enabled, where they constrained ambition and what remains unresolved.

gaps.title: Astrid lacks its own creative challenge culture
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; prior Banodoco competitions, but no established Astrid-specific program/outcome audit.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People have compelling reasons to attempt work beyond their current abilities: artistic challenges, collaboration, critiques, showcases and high standards that encourage originality and growth.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid builds on the existing Banodoco community, which has run art competitions including the [Arca Gidan Prize](https://arcagidan.com/). But **Astrid has not yet established a community centred on this tool and its artistic mission**, with a repeatable culture of challenges, critique and collective artistic growth. Earlier competitions provide experience and a starting point, not evidence that this new culture already exists.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The existing community experience has not yet become an Astrid-centred program of challenges, serious critique, recognition and feedback loops, judged by what people actually make rather than participation alone.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Run a bounded challenge with clear artistic intent and fair participation; document artists' goals, feedback, completed work and whether it enabled more ambitious efforts. Incorporate genuine creator assessment, including negative findings and barriers.

gaps.title: No implemented contributor-ownership model
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; earlier Banodoco arrangement lapsed, Astrid model and legal terms not established.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: The people who meaningfully advance the collective have a genuine, understandable stake in the company behind it. The stated ambition is **100% ownership for contributors advancing the mission**, not merely participation rewards.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Banodoco published a contributor-ownership approach, monthly grant lists and reported transfers. Its earlier proposal described splitting 1% per month over 8.5 years, with changing contributor categories and an explicitly provisional legal structure. The program has not been actively maintained during Astrid's recent development. **The historical publications are evidence of earlier commitments, not proof of legally issued equity.** An Astrid-specific arrangement must reconcile those records and existing promises before deciding new eligibility, allocation, governance, financing or implementation.
gaps.missingMarkdown: A transparent and legally workable mechanism for translating meaningful contributions—creative, technical, mentoring or otherwise—into ownership and rights, including treatment of existing and future financing, has not yet been specified or implemented.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An explicit owner decision and qualified legal/tax review of a concrete model covering eligible contributions, grants/allocations, governance, vesting, changes over time, financing and participant protections; then evidence of its authorized implementation. A declaration alone does not close this gap.

gaps.title: Agents don't yet reliably learn from creative work
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent routinely uses applicable earlier lessons **before** work, captures truthfully observed success or failure **during/after** work, learns within a user-owned private knowledge scope and can propose sanitized contributions to others with explicit permission.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has executable creative tools and Runtime task/artifact records. Banodoco Hivemind has an evidence-bearing read/contribution system. The [source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/inputs.md) **does not establish a complete private/local → community → later-agent learning loop**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Contextual retrieval, actual run-to-knowledge capture, safe private retention, consented contributions and proven benefits to a second agent session are not yet integrated end to end.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two real agent sessions: the first retrieves applicable knowledge and produces an observed, locally retained result; a subsequent session demonstrably uses that finding. Optional contribution retains provenance and only shares approved, sanitized information. Compare against raw search/no knowledge, including staleness and denial paths.

gaps.title: Independent Hiveminds don't yet work together
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Independent personal, team and community knowledge datasets can preserve attribution, conditions, evidence and owner-controlled access while exchanging permitted references and learnings without merging into one central authority.
gaps.currentMarkdown: [Banodoco Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/inputs.md) documents source-custodied messages, revisioned resources, an accepted search head and editorial contribution operations. The [uploaded October 29 protocol proposal](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/protocol-proposal.md) proposes dataset-scoped entries, typed links and `find`/`inspect`/`contribute`. **These are not yet identical proven contracts.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Versioned interoperable record/identity/reference and permission semantics, a local/private dataset implementation and one real cross-dataset boundary need a reconciled specification and evidence.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two separately owned datasets can exchange a scoped, independently attributed reference or approved sanitized result, preserving revision identity, provenance and access decisions; denied, stale and revoked cases do not leak source content. Banodoco behavior is preserved or safely, explicitly migrated with evidence.

gaps.title: Reliability isn't proven across supported setups
gaps.assessmentDetail: Partially evidenced (2026-11-06; source is existing plan/queue evidence, not a new qualification).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: On each declared supported operating system, device and deployment route, people can reliably install, launch, stop, update, roll back, repair and remove Astrid without losing projects or becoming stranded in an unexplained state. This concerns the application's **operational lifecycle**, not whether every creative workflow succeeds.
gaps.currentMarkdown:
[Plan 29](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/29-update-and-release/plan.md) is reopened: Release 10 (0.0.10) is published, but `install --update` on a machine that already completed the Release 1 storage handoff exits 0 and installs nothing. Less common setups remain in [Plan 30](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/30-update-everywhere/plan.md).


[Plan 08](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/08-release1-install-update/plan.md) records a completed five-row hosted R1 installation/update gate, proving that *specific* paths worked on *specific* candidates. The [project queue](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/README.md) records Plan 07 as active with indicative Pinokio evidence and existing CI failures, while Plans 09/10 target broader routes and native qualification. This is **not** proof that all devices, browser variants or real engines are covered.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Supported installation, launcher and engine lifecycle transitions—especially updates, failures, rollback, cleanup and recovery—still lack sufficiently broad, current and reproducible qualification. Creative job correctness belongs to F-003; authority over agent actions belongs to F-002.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A declared and version-pinned OS/device/deployment matrix demonstrates clean installation, launch, stop, update, interruption recovery, rollback and removal with preserved work and meaningful negative tests. This qualifies supported operational paths, not creative inference accuracy or permission policy.

gaps.title: User control and recovery aren't fully proven
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People can understand, grant, limit and revoke what Astrid and its agents may access, change, share or spend, and can recover safely from conflicting or rejected actions. Consequential changes, external effects and resource use follow explicit authority, and a refusal is respected. A sandbox is one safeguard, not the whole definition of creator control.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Runtime has versioned project/task authority and the App/Agent have meaningful editing and conflict primitives. [Plan 01](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/01-installer-consent/plan.md) is for installer choice; [Plan 04](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/04-concurrent-edits/plan.md) addresses concurrent edits; [Plan 15](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/15-openshell-safe-execution/plan.md) targets the independent [F-007 sandbox outcome](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/F-007-first-class-sandbox.md). These are different safeguards; together they **have not yet established this broader user-control outcome**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The user's authority over agent/tool actions, data access, external effects, concurrent editing and reversibility has not been proven coherently across representative real workflows. This is about **permissions, consent and control**, distinct from application installation/recovery (F-001) or whether a creative task produces the right result (F-003).
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Representative real workflows show clear and enforceable grant/deny/revoke permissions, correctly scoped file/network/spend access, handling of concurrent edits, inspectable changes, refusal and undo/recovery after failed or conflicting operations. Isolated execution has its own bounded closure test under F-007; passing it alone does not close this broader gap.

gaps.title: Creative execution isn't yet dependable end to end
gaps.desiredMarkdown: From a declared supported, usable Astrid workspace, a creator and agent can choose a creative operation, prepare an appropriate model or provider, execute real inference or media processing, and receive the intended **correct, editable creative result** with progress and recoverable failures. The core proof is successful creative work—not reinstalling or updating Astrid.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has Runtime execution/task primitives, packs, generation integrations and the video editor. [Plan 02](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/02-consistent-generation/plan.md) aims to establish consistent defaults and pinned stack on fixtures and a fresh Linux CPU setup, **explicitly not real inference**. [Plan 12](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/12-multiple-inference-routes/plan.md) targets real multiple inference routes. [Plan 20](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/20-zero-to-first-image/plan.md) targets a real first generated image on a timeline; [Plan 16](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/16-streamlined-agent-experience/plan.md) improves agent readiness.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The end-to-end **creative job**—capability selection, model/provider readiness, actual task execution, artifact identity and usable output—has not been dependably proven across selected supported workflows and failure paths. Install/update lifecycle belongs to F-001; approval and access decisions belong to F-002.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On a stated supported setup, run real creative generation or processing and inspect the resulting editable artifact for correct content, project identity, output settings and usable timeline/workspace integration. Demonstrate failed-job diagnostics, stop/retry and cleanup; separately qualify platform installation and permission boundaries in F-001/F-002.

gaps.title: Pack installation and upgrades aren't yet reliable
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Artists and agents can discover, install, enable, use, update, disable and safely roll back supported creative packs and their frontend/backend contributions. Compatibility, source identity, trust, ownership and project reference continuity remain understandable and reliable.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Agent has manifest-defined packs with actions, skills, UI and rendering contributions. App has trusted bundled extension lifecycle and editor SDK mechanisms. [Plan 06](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/06-packs/plan.md) explicitly targets pack extraction and reliable installation, trust, transaction, rendering and editor integration. [Plan 11](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/11-threejs-pack/plan.md) is a case of converting a first-party feature into a pack, but is not a generic workspace engine.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The practical lifecycle of reusable packs across Agent, Runtime and App still needs integrated, version-pinned proof of installation, runtime availability, use, safe upgrade/rollback, and handling of missing/broken contributions.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Install a supported pack, discover its declared actions/UI, use it on project data, update and roll back safely with exact pinned source identity; show missing dependencies, rejected/untrusted cases, recovery and no loss of project references. Do not claim arbitrary dynamically generated third-party code can run safely without independent isolation evidence.

gaps.title: Local-first projects can't yet use cloud execution seamlessly
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; remote routes exist but an integrated cloud-assisted local-files workflow has not been qualified.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator keeps **the Astrid project database and durable files on their own machine**, while consenting to an optional cloud agent session, remote image/video generation and remote video rendering. The agent handles provider selection, setup and execution within approved permissions and budgets; inputs sent to remote services are explicit and scoped. Results come back as correct editable files/operations in the same local workspace, with progress, cancellation, retry, recoverability and cleanup.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has local orchestration and selected provider/RunPod generation routes; [documented execution paths](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/main/docs/reference/where-things-run.md) distinguish provider APIs from local and RunPod inference. [Reigh Worker Orchestrator](https://github.com/banodoco/reigh-worker-orchestrator) documents RunPod worker and fal/Wavespeed API orchestration, but [the satellite-disposition review](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/main/tools/astrid-rename/satellites.md) marks that repository deprecated, with current deployment unverified. None of this establishes **an end-to-end Astrid cloud-agent + generation + render product** retaining local file/database authority.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Creators do not yet have a qualified, coherent way to delegate approved work from a locally owned Astrid project to cloud compute and return to that same editable project with clear consent, costs and recovery. The missing outcome is the reliable boundary between local custody and remote work—not a specific cloud provider, agent API or rendering service.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: With one approved provider/configuration and a declared local project, a user or their agent launches remote work (including image generation and a video render), watches status and costs, cancels/retries as appropriate, and receives correctly linked editable local artifacts with the **local database still authoritative**. A qualification report covers data actually transmitted, permissions, cleanup, non-success paths, security boundaries and retention. Offline/unsupported cases are identified honestly.

gaps.title: Creators can't yet work in Astrid entirely from the cloud
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; no qualified fully hosted project/database/media lifecycle.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator can use Astrid from a browser without maintaining a local install. The hosted workspace owns persistent project/database state, files/media, accounts and access controls, while cloud agents, generation and video rendering execute under explicit authorization and clear budgets. Projects can be exported or migrated back into user custody; reliable backup, restore, isolation and deletion are supported.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has a browser-capable App, Runtime and cloud/provider execution paths, but the [Cloud-assisted V1 plan](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/25-cloud-assist-v1/plan.md) deliberately **keeps durable files and project database local**. An always-available hosted tenancy, canonical cloud database, durable object storage and migration/recovery contract are not qualified.
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no qualified way to start a creative project, keep its working state and files, and return to it in a browser without maintaining a local Astrid install. Durable, account-scoped access, recovery and export are part of that user outcome; the particular database, storage and hosting architecture are choices for implementing it, not the definition of the gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A new user can open a hosted Astrid workspace in a browser, create a project, save and reopen across sessions/devices, run a generation and render, and observe durable, permission-scoped data; accounts are isolated. Backup/restore, quota, delete, export/migration and interrupted execution are tested. A local-first/offline option remains a distinct supported route rather than being silently replaced.

gaps.title: Running Astrid in a sandbox isn't yet a first-class option
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; sandbox foundations exist, but an integrated, qualified user-facing full-stack path has not been demonstrated (2026-11-07).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People can choose to run Astrid's creative environment—App, Agent, Runtime and permitted tools—in an isolated sandbox as a normal, understandable setup option. They can grant and revoke access to host files, credentials, network destinations, external inference services and compute resources without needing to manage low-level containment themselves. They can work, stop and recover predictably, and understand any integrations that cross the isolation boundary.
gaps.currentMarkdown: There is relevant ongoing work: [Astrid Agent PR #109](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/pull/109) contains OpenShell sandbox setup and controls, and [Plan 15](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/15-openshell-safe-execution/plan.md) covers an integrated full-stack option. Current Agent sources include sandbox scripts, but their existence does not demonstrate a supported, first-class end-to-end user experience or verified isolation across the App, Agent and Runtime. The PR was open when checked on 2026-11-07; environment and platform qualification remain to be established.
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no proven, user-friendly path for selecting, starting and using a **fully isolated Astrid workspace** with understandable permissions and boundaries. The outcome is independent of a particular sandbox technology: OpenShell is one possible implementation, not the definition of the gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On a declared supported platform, a user can choose the sandbox mode, start the required stack, perform an approved creative job, stop and restart, and recover their project. Show positive and negative checks for permissions to host files/credentials, network and external inference, including denied actions, cancellation and safe teardown. Document what runs inside versus outside, any opted-in host integration, and residual risks. This proves a bounded supported isolation option, not universal security or a complete answer to [the broader user-control gap F-002](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/F-002-safe-user-control.md).

gaps.title: Generation isn't yet one portable, extensible path across machines and inference engines
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; path review and live RunPod attempts (2026-11-08).
gaps.desiredMarkdown:
Any generation, in any modality (image, edit, video, voice, music, sound effects and composed workflows such as h3_av), runs through **one path**:
1. Declare what the request needs: custom nodes and models.
2. Choose where it runs once: this machine and a chosen local GPU, a user's own server, or a rented GPU machine such as RunPod. There is a default the creator sets and can change per generation.
3. Optionally bring that machine in line with the needs (align, only check, or trust what is there).
4. Run it on the chosen inference engine. ComfyUI through VibeComfy comes first; others such as Wan2GP follow.
5. Get the result back.

A rented machine behaves like any other machine: it runs the same path. It can be reused while warm, and it keeps models on attached storage so they are downloaded once. **Every level is a replaceable piece**, extended through a declared contract rather than a core change:
- **workflows:** a VibeComfy plugin adds templates such as h3_av;
- **engines:** ComfyUI, Wan2GP;
- **machines and providers:** local GPU, a user's server, RunPod, another rented-GPU provider.

Adding one reuses the rest of the path rather than adding per-modality or per-pack routes.
gaps.currentMarkdown:
- **On RunPod, live attempts on 7–8 Nov 2026 produced image and edit; voice and music did not produce an output.**
  - Placement is re-decided in several places.
  - A rented pod is driven as a remote ComfyUI, so checks ran against the controller's disk.
  - Every fresh pod downloads one fixed 95.8 GB model bundle, whatever the job.
  - Pods can't be reused across jobs, and the storage volume is used only off the main path.
- **Some slots don't follow the common path.**
  - Sound effects is refused on RunPod.
  - h3_av has its own pod route.
  - About 50 sites branch by modality.
- **Building blocks exist but are not on one path.** VibeComfy already offers requirements, node install, model fetch and run commands that the Agent partly duplicates.
- **Only one engine works.** Wan2GP is a stub.

The evidence is the merge-run path review in `banodoco/astrid-overnight-2026-11-05`, branch `merge-run/2026-11-07`, `merge-run/path-review/` (VISION, HOLISTIC, EXISTING-MACHINERY and the audits).
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no single, engine-neutral generation path whose placement is decided once, and its levels (workflows, engines, machines) can't yet be extended independently. Creators can't freely choose and change where a generation runs, or which inference engine runs it, and get the same behaviour, setup and result every time. Distinct from [F-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/F-003-creative-execution.md), which is about one creative job being dependable end to end on a stated setup, and from [F-005](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/F-005-local-files-cloud-assist.md), which is about the local-data and cloud-execution product boundary.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown:
**Same request, different machines.** The same generation request, for every default slot plus h3_av, produces its result through the same code path on:
- a local GPU;
- a user's own ComfyUI;
- a rented RunPod machine.

**Placement is one decision.** A default placement is set and overridden for a single generation.

**Rented machines are efficient.**
- A second job reuses a warm machine.
- Models already on attached storage are not downloaded again.
- Align, check and trust behave the same everywhere.

**Each level extends independently.**
- A second inference engine (Wan2GP) runs a generation through the same placement, lease and machine route, adding only its own setup and run step.
- A workflow added as a VibeComfy plugin (h3_av) runs with no plugin-specific code in Astrid's core.
- A further kind of machine or provider can be added behind the same placement and lease contract, shown at least with a test provider, without changing the path.

**One path in the code.** Source inspection shows one placement decision site, one submit and one retrieve, and no per-modality branch on the path.

**Negative cases:** a missing model fails before submit, naming the machine; an expired lease releases the machine; no orphaned machine remains.

gaps.title: Creative components can't yet move freely
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Real creative components (timeline, player, inspector, gallery and others) can move, dock, resize, float and nest within a declarative workspace without losing their state, supported behavior or resource bindings.
gaps.currentMarkdown: The [App source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/24-liquid-workspace/inputs.md) identifies actual reusable editor views and a custom two-pane assembly. The standard editor shell still includes host-specific layout, gesture and context responsibilities. **This does not establish a general-purpose portable workspace host.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Component definitions, instances, presentation/lifecycle and positioning are not yet proven independently composable across workspace layouts and domains.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Rearrange the **real** player, inspector and timeline; retain playback, editing, selection and recovery state; save/restore the layout. Then host a genuinely different domain component using the same contract, without modifying the main editor shell.

gaps.title: Agents can't yet reconfigure the workspace
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent and a person use the same supported workspace operations to open, place, attach, bind, focus and restore component instances. Changes are inspectable, scoped, reversible and compatible with live creative work.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has pack/skill/action discovery. Astrid App has extensions, commands and scoped editing contexts. The [source review](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/24-liquid-workspace/inputs.md) has **not** established a public, domain-neutral workspace manipulation API.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Spatial **placement/attachment** and functional **resource binding** need explicit, validated operations; proximity alone must not silently connect data. Agents should compose existing software without generating frontend code for ordinary layout changes.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An agent arranges the same real components as a user, binds the correct timeline/selection/clock, offers reversible operations, does not clobber user edits, and restores a prior workspace from a saved representation.

gaps.title: Frontend and backend extensions don't yet compose
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator or agent can discover and use one pack's creative capability, its typed results and its appropriate frontend components together—extending opinionated tools without bespoke, duplicate integrations.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent pack manifests can declare actions, UI, renderers and skills. Astrid App has a video-editor extension SDK, typed data lanes, proposals and rendering hooks. Current pack UI hosting is still tied to supported host entries; **general component-owned extension points and unified live composition are unproven**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Common identity and discovery across pack contributions, semantic resource/result bindings, component-defined extension hosts and safe activation need proving beyond the default video editor.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An installed/trusted music capability yields a typed beat-grid result used in a real timeline view and music control surface. The interface can be rearranged, results correctly track source-to-timeline coordinates, and updates follow existing authoritative domain editing/undo. A second distinct extension domain validates generality.

gaps.title: A creative ecosystem across modalities isn't yet established
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; vision and draft-plan assessment (2026-11-07), not a qualification of current product coverage.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Astrid grows into an open ecosystem of powerful, agent-native, deeply extensible creative foundations across video, images, music, 3D and further modalities. The collective and independent contributors can create, publish, adapt and maintain these foundations; other people and agents can build additional tools and capabilities on top of them, combine them and make ambitious work without forking Astrid's core. Video is a deliberate starting point, not a limit on the underlying philosophy.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid is primarily a video editor and timeline, with generation, packs, agent protocols and other supporting capabilities. Video is an exciting medium to establish a strong foundation, but the existing product and its interfaces remain video-centered. [Packs](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/06-packs/plan.md), [VibeComfy extensibility](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/17-vibecomfy-extensibility/plan.md), [timeline foundations](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/18-timeline-editing/plan.md), [Three.js extraction](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/11-threejs-pack/plan.md) and [liquid workspaces](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/plans/24-liquid-workspace/plan.md) are related implementation directions, not evidence of a flourishing cross-modal ecosystem.
gaps.missingMarkdown: It is not yet demonstrated that people can establish and share **reusable modality-level foundations** beyond video, or that independent contributors can build on those foundations to create further creative tools. This is broader than [LS-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/LS-003-full-stack-contributions.md), which concerns composable frontend/backend extension contracts within a working host; it is also distinct from proving one artist's end-to-end workflow under [AA-001](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/10ad6ee3e615b05e160aba16ae55626ab9a23983/vision/gaps/AA-001-sustained-creative-work.md).
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On documented supported setups, creators and agents successfully make real work using video plus at least two non-video modality foundations, with preserved files and project control. At least one non-video foundation is contributed outside the core team, and another independent contributor can build and publish a useful additional capability on top of it without a bespoke core fork. Show actual creative results; discoverability, setup, shared agent/user interfaces, extension and update paths, permissions, recovery and meaningful negative cases; and feedback from creators who use these tools. This demonstrates a reusable cross-modal ecosystem, **not** a claim that every imaginable modality has been completed.

projects.title: One update path and release

projects.title: Zero-to-first-image onboarding

Setup choices stay visible and changeable on the agent path. The skill uses an existing ComfyUI, installs an engine on a capable machine, or rents RunPod otherwise.

projects.title: One generation path

projects.goalMarkdown: One optional `destination` on the generate request (SDK and CLI) makes the result a variant of an existing generation, promotes it to main, and places it on the timeline at a given time and track, with no follow-up calls; refusals come before any work, and a failed timeline step keeps the generation and names the exact retry.

projects.title: One home for user state
projects.goalMarkdown: User choices, project choices and project work live in the Runtime (app-state and project documents), not in side files, env variables or browser storage; machine bootstrap state stays local.

projects.title: One credential path
projects.goalMarkdown: Every secret Astrid uses (fal, provider keys, RunPod token) is stored, granted and revoked through the Runtime's credential records, never in plain env files or settings.

projects.title: Install and update confidence

projects.title: Pinokio qualification
